# Twintrinsic — LLMs.txt

A machine-readable digest of the Twintrinsic Svelte component library documentation and API.

## Component Reference


### Accordion/Accordion

Accordion - A group of collapsible panels using native HTML details/summary elements. By default, only one panel can be open at a time using the native `name` attribute. Usage: ```svelte Section 1 Content for section 1 Section 2 Content for section 2 ```

### Accordion/AccordionItem

AccordionItem - Individual item within an Accordion component. Uses native HTML details/summary elements for semantic disclosure. Usage: ```svelte Section Title Content goes here ```

### Alert/Alert

Alert - A component for displaying inline alerts, important information, or warnings. Colored background with a thick one-side border. Use for "You have 3 new messages", "Your account is almost full", informational callouts, or best-practices sections. Usage: ```svelte A new version is available. Your storage is 95% full. Upgrade your plan to add more space. Profile saved successfully. Something went wrong. Please try again. ```

### AppHeader/AppHeader

AppHeader - A responsive application header with navigation, actions, and branding. Supports mobile menu, search, notifications, and user profile. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Avatar/Avatar

Avatar - A component for displaying user profile images with fallback options. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Avatar/AvatarGroup

AvatarGroup - A component for displaying multiple avatars in a compact, overlapping layout. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and overflow handling. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Badge/Badge

Badge - A component for displaying small counts, status indicators, or labels. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte New 42 Online Notifications 5 ```

### BottomBar/BottomBar

BottomBar - A panel that attaches to the bottom of its parent container. Useful as a mobile app bar, media-player controls, a console/detail panel, or any bar that should be available on demand. Visibility is driven by the `expanded` prop so the bar can be shown/hidden from another component's UX (e.g. shown when a mobile menu opens). When the `collapsible` prop is set, the header also acts as a toggle: clicking it slides the panel down to a small handle, and clicking the handle slides it back in. For a static bar, visibility is prop-driven: bind `expanded` to app state and update it from `ontoggle` (e.g. a mobile menu button). For a collapsible detail panel, set `collapsible` and click the header to slide the bar down to a handle. Usage: ```svelte Details Content here Details Content here ```

### Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb

Breadcrumb - A navigation component that helps users understand their location in a website or application. Provides a hierarchical trail of links with proper accessibility features. Usage: ```svelte Home Products Current Page Home Documentation Components ```

### Breadcrumb/BreadcrumbItem

BreadcrumbItem - An individual item within a Breadcrumb component. Renders as a link when href is provided, otherwise as a span for the current page. Usage: ```svelte Home ... "> Products Current Page ```

### Button/Button

Button - A styled button component with various variants and sizes. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and loading states. Usage: ```svelte Default Button Primary Button Settings About Us ```

### Button/ButtonGroup

ButtonGroup - A component for grouping related buttons together. Provides consistent styling and spacing for button collections. Usage: ```svelte Left Middle Right Top Middle Bottom ```

### Card/Card

Card - A container for content with optional header, footer, and media sections. Provides a consistent visual style for displaying grouped information. Snippets: header, footer, media, children. If both `media` snippet and `image` prop are passed, the `media` snippet takes precedence.

### Carousel/Carousel

Carousel - A component for displaying slideshows of content. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte Slide 1 content Slide 2 content Slide 3 content ```

### Carousel/CarouselItem

CarouselItem - An individual slide within a Carousel component. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and transition effects. Usage: ```svelte Slide Title Slide content goes here ```

### CodeBlock/CodeBlock

CodeBlock - A component for displaying code snippets with syntax highlighting and copy functionality. Features: - Syntax highlighting with Prism.js - Automatic language detection - Dynamic language loading via Prism.js autoloader plugin - Copy to clipboard functionality - Support for multiple CDNs (unpkg, esm.sh, jsdelivr) > NOTE: The slot needs to be outdented as far as possible so the child contents' first line isn't indented. Usage: ```svelte const hello = 'world'; console.log(hello); <!-- Auto-detects language --> const hello = 'world'; print('hello world') <!-- Custom CDN and language path --> const code = 'example'; ```

### CompatibilityMatrix/CompatibilityMatrix

CompatibilityMatrix - renders a cross-browser support table for the Tier 0 "Chrome-only" platform APIs tracked in docs/plans/HTML_SEMANTIC_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.md. Data is generated by `pnpm test:compat` (Playwright, run against Chromium/Firefox/WebKit — see tests/compat/browser-support.test.ts) and merged into `static/browser-compat.json` by scripts/merge-browser-compat.mjs. This component fetches that file at runtime, so the matrix always reflects the last time the compat suite ran in CI without requiring a rebuild of the docs site. Usage: ```svelte import CompatibilityMatrix from "$lib/components/CompatibilityMatrix/CompatibilityMatrix.svelte" // Show every tracked feature // Show only the features relevant to one component ```

### Container/Container

Container - A base layout component that provides consistent padding, width, and responsive behavior. Serves as the foundation for other layout components. Usage: ```svelte Content Full-width content ```

### DataTable/DataTable

DataTable - A component for displaying tabular data with advanced features. Provides sorting, filtering, pagination, and selection capabilities with proper accessibility. Usage: ```svelte ```

### DocPage/DocPage

DocPage — Standardized documentation page layout for all Twintrinsic component pages. Enforces a consistent section ordering: Name → Description → What/When/Why → Responsiveness → Customization → Examples → Slots → Props → Events → Accessibility → Keyboard Support. Every section is an optional snippet — only rendered when provided. This makes the component backward-compatible: existing pages can adopt sections one at a time. Usage: ```svelte A versatile interactive element. What is it? A styled button component. Click me `}> Click me ```

### DocPage/DocSection

DocSection — A reusable documentation section with consistent heading and spacing. Use this inside DocPage or standalone for sub-sections, comparison tables, and callouts that need consistent styling. Usage: ```svelte Tags are interactive and selectable; badges are decorative. Use primary variant for main CTAs ```

### EventsTable/EventsTable

EventsTable - renders a component's events (Svelte 5 `on*` callback props) as a documentation table. Data source, in order of precedence: 1. `component` — pass a component module (namespace import) that exports a `propsMetadata` array; EventsTable reads it directly and keeps the entries whose `eventDetail` is set. 2. `data` — a plain hash of ` ` (names are written without the `on` prefix). If neither yields data, EventsTable logs a `console.warn` and renders nothing. Usage: ```svelte import * as Calendar from "twintrinsic/components/Calendar" import EventsTable from "twintrinsic/components/EventsTable" ```

### Footer/Footer

Footer - A flexible footer component with left, center, and right regions. ## Props - `class` - Additional CSS classes - `left` - Left-aligned content snippet - `center` - Center-aligned content snippet - `right` - Right-aligned content snippet ## Usage ```svelte © 2024 Company } center= right= /> Copyright © 2024 QuestLists } /> ```

### Form/AutoComplete

AutoComplete - An input component that provides suggestions as you type. Built on top of the base Input component with additional dropdown functionality. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Calendar

Calendar - A date picker built on the native ` ` element. Uses the browser's built-in date picker for accessibility, validation, and localized formatting — free of charge. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Checkbox

Checkbox - A form component for boolean or indeterminate input with customizable labels, descriptions, and validation states. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/ColorPicker

ColorPicker - A color selection component built on the native ` ` element. Provides the browser's built-in color picker with a text input for direct hex entry. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Combobox

Combobox - A component that combines a text input with a dropdown list. Provides autocomplete functionality with keyboard navigation and accessibility features. The dropdown is a native `popover="auto"` element (top layer, light-dismiss, Esc-to-close) positioned with CSS Anchor Positioning (`anchor-name` / `position-anchor` / `anchor()`), so no JS measures the input width or manages outside-click/Esc. Load `loadPlatformPolyfills()` in the host app to restore these behaviors in engines without native support. Usage: ```svelte console.log(e.detail.value)} /> console.log(e.detail.value)} />

### Form/Dropdown

Dropdown - A wrapper around Select for backward compatibility. All functionality is now in Select. Use Select directly for new code. This component is deprecated. Use Select instead: ```svelte ```

### Form/FileUpload

FileUpload - A component for uploading files with drag and drop support. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte Drag files here or click to browse ```

### Form/FloatLabel

FloatLabel - A component for creating form inputs with animated floating labels. Provides a modern, space-efficient input with improved user experience. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Form

Form - A component for creating accessible, styled forms with validation support. Handles form submission, validation, and provides context for form controls. Usage: ```svelte Submit ```

### Form/FormBuilder

FormBuilder - Generates an accessible form from an OpenAPI 3.0 schema or an explicit field-descriptor array. Maps schema types onto Twintrinsic form controls: string -> TextInput (email/password via `format`), enum -> Select, integer/number -> NumberInput, boolean -> Switch, array -> ListInput (or a multi-select when the items are enumerated), object -> a nested fieldset group. Required fields, descriptions, defaults, and numeric bounds all flow through to the generated controls, and the whole thing renders inside a ` ` so native validation and the submit payload work out of the box. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/FormField

FormField - A component for creating form field containers with labels, validation, and help text. Provides consistent styling and accessibility features for form inputs. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Input

Input - Base component for form inputs with validation, floating labels, and input groups. Built with accessibility and customization in mind. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/InputSwitch

InputSwitch - Deprecated alias for Switch. Use Switch instead. This component re-exports Switch for backward compatibility. New code should use Switch directly.

### Form/InvalidState

InvalidState - A component for displaying validation errors in forms. Provides consistent styling and accessibility features for error messages. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Knob

Knob - A circular progress slider component for selecting numeric values. Provides an intuitive circular interface with drag interaction and keyboard controls. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/ListInput

ListInput - A component for handling multiple input values displayed as "chips". Allows adding, removing, and editing multiple values with keyboard navigation. Usage: ```svelte /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(value)} errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address" /> ```

### Form/Listbox

Listbox - A component for selecting one or multiple options from a list. Provides accessible keyboard navigation, filtering, and customization options. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/NumberInput

NumberInput - A specialized input for numeric values with formatting, units, and increment controls. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and integration with the Form component. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Radio

Radio - A styled radio button component. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and integration with the Form component. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/RadioGroup

RadioGroup - A component for grouping related radio buttons. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and integration with the Form component. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/Rating

Rating - A component for collecting user ratings through stars or other symbols. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and interactive options. ## Features - **Value binding**: Two-way binding with `value` prop, synced to hidden number input - **Min/Max constraints**: Native HTML5 number input handles validation with `min`, `max`, and `step` attributes - **Step control**: `step` prop sets the granularity (e.g., 0.5 for half-stars, 1 for whole stars) - matches HTML number input API - **Visual customization**: Configurable size (sm, md, lg) and color variant (default, primary, secondary, success, warning, error, info) - **Custom icons**: Use named icons (e.g., "star", "heart") via Icon component or custom snippets for full control - **Interactive modes**: Full interactivity, readonly, or disabled states - matches HTML number input API - **Hover preview**: Optional `showPreview` to display hover values before committing - **Numeric display**: `showValue` prop to show the current rating number - **Drag support**: Mouse and touch drag to set value across the component - **Keyboard navigation**: Arrow keys (±step), Home (min), End (max) for accessibility - **Form integration**: Hidden number input with `name`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `disabled` attributes for form submission - **Accessibility**: Full ARIA support (slider role, valuemin/max/now, labels) and keyboard navigation - **Events**: `onchange` callback fires when value is committed, `onhover` fires during preview - **Standard API**: Exposes the same attributes as HTML ` ` (min, max, step, name, placeholder, readonly, disabled) Usage: ```svelte console.log(e.detail.value)} /> ```

### Form/Select

Select - A native HTML select component for selecting options from a dropdown list. Supports single and multiple selection with optgroup for nested options. Uses `appearance: base-select` (Chrome 135+) for customizable styling with a styled picker, arrow icon, and option checkmarks. Falls back to the standard OS dropdown in browsers without support. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Form/SelectGroup

SelectGroup - A component for grouping related options in a Select component. Provides semantic grouping with optional labels. Usage: ```svelte France Germany United States Canada ```

### Form/Slider

Slider - A component for selecting values from a range. Uses native HTML input[type="range"] with consistent styling and accessibility. Usage: ```svelte console.log(e.detail.value)} /> ```

### Form/Switch

Switch - A toggle switch component that provides an alternative to checkboxes. Supports labels, disabled states, and integrates with the Form component. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Icon/Icon

Icon - A wrapper around @iconify/svelte that uses the global iconset configuration. This component allows you to use Iconify icons with a globally configured default iconset. Users can set the default iconset once and all Icon components will use it. Usage: ```svelte import from 'twintrinsic' setIconset('mdi-light') <!-- Uses default iconset (mdi-light) --\> <!-- Override for specific icon --\> <!-- With custom styling --\> ```

### Lazy/Lazy

Lazy - A component that renders its content only when it becomes visible in the viewport. Useful for performance optimization by deferring the rendering of off-screen content. Usage: ```svelte This content will only be rendered when visible Loading... }> ```

### Lazy/LazyPanel

LazyPanel - A Panel that only renders its body once it becomes visible in the viewport. Useful for expandable panels holding lazy content. Usage: ```svelte Lazy Content Loading... ```

### LocaleSwitcher/LocaleSwitcher

LocaleSwitcher - A language picker that switches the active Paraglide locale. Renders either a group of toggle buttons or a native , driven by the Paraglide runtime (`getLocale`/`setLocale`). Language names are shown in their own language (e.g. "Español", "فارسی") so every option stays readable regardless of the active locale. Requires Paraglide-JS compiled to `$lib/paraglide` with the same locales listed in `messages/ .json` (this repo's setup — see the vite plugin and `project.inlang/settings.json`). Usage: ```svelte ```

### Masonry/Masonry

Masonry - A component for creating Pinterest-style grid layouts. Provides responsive, dynamic layouts for items of varying heights. Usage: ```svelte Item 1 with some content Item 2 with more content that might be taller Item 3 with less content Item 4 with a different height

### Menu/Menu/Menu

Menu - A dropdown menu component using the native Popover API with CSS Anchor Positioning. Renders a trigger button and a popover content panel positioned relative to the trigger. Supports full WAI-ARIA keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter, Esc, Home/End). Usage: ```svelte Open Menu Option 1 Option 2 ```

### Metrics/DonutChart/DonutChart

DonutChart — Backward-compatible wrapper around PieChart with `hole= `. Prefer using ` ` directly for new code.

### Metrics/LineChart/LineChart

LineChart — An SVG line chart with multiple series, grid lines, and legend. Supports line smoothing (smooth, step), hover tooltips, and click interactivity.

### Metrics/PieChart/PieChart

PieChart — An SVG pie chart for displaying proportional data. Supports donut mode via the `hole` prop, custom start angle, counter-clockwise direction, center text, hover tooltips, click interactivity, and keyboard navigation.

### Metrics/ProgressMetric/ProgressMetric

ProgressMetric — A labeled progress bar for displaying metric values. Delegates to the Progress component with label, tooltip, and percentage display. Usage: ```svelte ``` > **Note:** Prefer using ` ` directly for new code. ProgressMetric is maintained > for backward compatibility.

### Modal/Modal

Modal - A dialog component for displaying content that requires user attention. Built on the native HTML ` ` element with `closedby="any"` for built-in light-dismiss (Esc + backdrop click + platform close gestures), native focus management, inert background content, and `@starting-style` + `allow-discrete` entry/exit animations. No manual focus trap, backdrop div, or Escape listener. Usage: ```svelte showModal = false}> Modal Title Modal content goes here showModal = false}>Close Save ```

### Panel/Card

Card - A styled container for content with optional header and footer. Built on top of the Panel component with additional card-specific styling. Usage: ```svelte Card Title Card content Card footer Title Content with hover effect

### Panel/LazyPanel

LazyPanel - A Panel component that only loads its content when it becomes visible in the viewport. Built on top of the Panel component with intersection observer for lazy loading. Usage: ```svelte Lazy Content Loading... ```

### Panel/Panel

Panel - A collapsible container with header and content sections. Provides smooth animations and keyboard accessibility. Usage: ```svelte Panel Title Content goes here Settings Settings content ```

### Progress/Progress

Progress - A component for displaying progress bars using native HTML progress element. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte `$ %`} /> ```

### PropsTable/PropsTable

PropsTable - renders a component's props as a documentation table. Data source, in order of precedence: 1. `component` — pass a component module (namespace import) that exports a `propsMetadata` array; PropsTable reads it directly. 2. `data` — a plain hash of ` `. If neither yields data, PropsTable logs a `console.warn` and renders nothing. Self-describing component convention: ```svelte export const propsMetadata = [ , ]; ``` Usage: ```svelte import * as Button from "twintrinsic/components/Button" import PropsTable from "twintrinsic/components/PropsTable" ```

### Section/Section

Section - A themed content section container for one-page websites and page layouts. Provides consistent theming with optional header, subtitle, and customizable borders/backgrounds. Usage: We love you and you love we! Custom title content Custom subtitle content We love you and you love we!

### Separator/Separator

Separator - A visual divider that can be horizontal or vertical with optional text/icon content. Usage: ```svelte or Featured Content ```

### Sidebar/Sidebar

Sidebar - A responsive side panel that adapts to screen size. - Mobile: Hidden by default, controlled by parent via `visible` prop - Tablet: Shows only icons (collapsed width via CSS) - Desktop: Shows full width with labels ## Props - `visible` - Show/hide the sidebar (controlled by parent) (default: false) - `position` - Sidebar position: "left" or "right" (default: "left") - `width` - Width of the sidebar on desktop when fully expanded (default: "16rem") - `collapsedWidth` - Width of the sidebar on tablet (icon-only mode) (default: "4rem") - `id` - Custom element ID (default: random UUID) - `ariaLabel` - Accessibility label for the sidebar - `disabled` - Disable toggle functionality (default: false) - `class` - Additional CSS classes - `menu` - Menu items array for SidebarMenu component (optional) - `onvisibilitychange` - Callback when sidebar visibility changes - `ontoggle` - Callback when sidebar is toggled (for desktop expand/collapse) ## Slots - `header` - Header content for the Panel - `default` - Main sidebar content ## Responsive Behavior - Mobile (< 768px): Hidden unless `visible= `, controlled by parent - Tablet (768px - 1024px): Shows with `collapsedWidth` (icons only) - Desktop (> 1024px): Shows with full `width` ## Usage ```svelte showMobileMenu = e.visible}> Menu will be rendered using SidebarMenu ```

### Skeleton/Skeleton

Skeleton - A component for displaying loading placeholders. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various shapes for content loading states. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Splitter/Splitter

Splitter - A resizable divider component that allows users to drag and adjust the width/height of two adjacent containers. Usage: ```svelte Left content Right content ``` ## A11y note The divider follows the [W3C APG window-splitter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/) (`role="separator"` + `tabindex="0"` + `aria-valuenow/min/max` + keyboard handlers). Svelte 5's static analysis flags this as `a11y_no_noninteractive_tabindex` because `separator` is classified as a non-interactive role. The `role`, `tabindex`, and event listeners are set at runtime via the `separator` Svelte action to bypass the false positive. If Svelte updates its role classifications, move these attributes back into the template.

### Stepper/Stepper

Stepper - A component for displaying multi-step processes or wizards. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte Account details Profile information Review and submit Step 1 content Step 2 content Step 3 content Step 4 content ```

### Stepper/StepperStep

StepperStep - An individual step within a Stepper component. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and various display options. Usage: ```svelte Content for the account details step ... " completed > Review step content Payment step content ```

### Table/Table

Table - A component for displaying structured data in rows and columns. Provides accessible, responsive tables with sorting, selection, and pagination options. Usage: ```svelte Name Email Role John Doe john@example.com Admin <!-- More rows --\> ```

### Table/TableBody

TableBody - A component for the body section of a Table. Provides consistent styling for the table body. Usage: ```svelte <!-- Table header content --\> John Doe john@example.com <!-- More rows --\> ```

### Tabs/Tab

Tab - An individual tab button within a TabList component. Provides the clickable interface for selecting tab panels. Usage: ```svelte Tab Label Disabled Tab ... "> Tab with Icon ```

### Tabs/TabPanel

TabPanel - A container for tab content within a Tabs component. Displays content when its corresponding Tab is selected. Usage: ```svelte Content for the first tab This content only renders when the tab is selected ```

### ThemeToggle/ThemeToggle

ThemeToggle - A toggle button for switching between light and dark themes. Supports keyboard interaction and ARIA labels. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Timer/Timer

Timer - A countdown/count-up display with pause/resume/reset controls. Renders a large monospace readout backed by one of three display variants (Progress bar, GaugeChart, or KPICard) plus optional built-in controls. Usage: ```svelte ```

### Tree/TreeNode

TreeNode - An individual node within a Tree component. Provides consistent styling, accessibility features, and keyboard navigation. Usage: ```svelte ... " expanded selected disabled > ```

### TreeMenu/TreeMenu

TreeMenu - A hierarchical menu component using native HTML / elements. Provides semantic, accessible tree navigation with minimal JavaScript. ## Props - `items` - Array of menu items with optional children, icons, and links - `class` - Additional CSS classes - `showSearch` - Whether to show search/filter input (default: false) ## Menu Item Structure ```typescript ``` ## Usage ```svelte ```

## Documentation Pages


### /docs/

Documentation home page

Twintrinsic Documentation Welcome to the Twintrinsic documentation. Twintrinsic is a collection of accessible, customizable components built with Svelte 5 and Tailwind CSS. Installation Required Tailwind setup Twintrinsic is styled with Tailwind CSS v4. The library's theme file (twintrinsic/twintrinsic.css) imports tailwindcss and declares the official @tailwindcss/forms and @tailwindcss/typography plugins via @plugin, so consumer apps must install those packages (they are not bundled): Then wire up the Tailwind Vite plugin. Components use lang="postcss" styles with @reference, so the Svelte plugin needs its preprocessor: Usage Import the library CSS once, then import components from the root barrel or from subpath exports (deep imports keep your bundle small): Features Built with Svelte 5 and Tailwind CSS Fully accessible components with ARIA support Responsive design with mobile-first approach Dark mode support out of the box Customizable theming TypeScript support Twintrinsic provides a set of essential components to build modern web applications: Layout Components Container - Responsive container with consistent padding AppHeader - Application header with navigation Sidebar - Collapsible side panel BottomBar - Collapsible bottom panel UI Components Panel - Collapsible content panel ButtonDropdown - Accessible dropdown menu Separator - Visual divider with optional content Twintrinsic uses CSS variables for theming. You can customize the look and feel by overriding these variables in your CSS: Dark Mode Dark mode is supported out of the box. Add the following to your CSS to customize dark mode colors: To avoid a brief flash of light mode on load, see the Theming for the required app.html initializer.

### /docs/completion

Completion and development process documentation

Development Completion This page documents the development process and completion status of the Twintrinsic component library. Development Process Development Approach Twintrinsic was developed using various tools and LLMs. The main IDE is Windsurf/Devin with Claude Haiku 4.5+ and SWE-1.6+ as an AI pair programmer. I have also used freebuff when I needed to clean up A LOT of code at once, mainly fixing svelte/ts errors that the other LLMs introduced and adding tests. The development process leveraged AI assistance for: Component Generation - Initial component scaffolding and implementation Unit Tests - Vitest-based unit tests for component functionality E2E Tests - Playwright-based end-to-end tests within Storybook stories Storybook Stories - Interactive component documentation and testing Demo Site Documentation - Usage examples and API documentation Manual Updates and Refinements While AI assistance was invaluable for generating initial code, they generate poor code and build components using old technology, sometimes building full components from scratch where standard HTML components we can use already exist (like a dropdown component). All components are manually reviewed and updated to ensure they use modern web APIs and best practices. This is necessary due to: Outdated Training Data - LLM training data has a knowledge cutoff, missing recent API improvements LLM Inaccuracies - AI-generated code may contain subtle bugs or suboptimal patterns Modern API Adoption - Components have been updated to use modern browser APIs like the Popover API and HTML Dialog elements 2026 Best Practices - Styling and component patterns have been refined to match current web development standards Key Updates Migration from createEventDispatcher to callback props (Svelte 5 pattern) Implementation of modern dialog and popover APIs where applicable Enhanced accessibility with WCAG 2.1 compliance Refined Tailwind CSS styling with semantic color naming Improved TypeScript type safety and JSDoc documentation Browser Compatibility Twintrinsic targets current Chrome first, since Chrome tends to ship new platform APIs before other engines and most non-Firefox/Safari browsers are Chromium-derived. That said, we aim for roughly 80% Firefox compatibility on the Tier 0 platform APIs from docs/plans/HTML_SEMANTIC_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.md . The table below is generated by running the same feature-detection probe in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit via Playwright ( pnpm test:compat ) and is not hand-maintained. Component Completion Checklist The following checklist indicates which components have been manually reviewed and updated with modern APIs and best practices: Next Steps As components are manually reviewed and updated, check them off in the list above. This ensures that all components meet the quality standards and use modern APIs appropriate for 2026 web development.

### /docs/components

Components overview page

Components Twintrinsic provides a set of accessible, customizable components built with Svelte 5 and Tailwind CSS. Each component is responsive and follows best practices for accessibility.

### /docs/components/Accordion/Accordion

Accordion documentation page — standardized structure

Accordion Accordion is a group of collapsible items where only one can be expanded at a time by default. It uses native <details> / <summary> elements for semantic disclosure, with full keyboard navigation and ARIA support. What, When & Why What is it? A disclosure widget group that lets users expand and collapse sections of content. It uses the native HTML <details> element with a name attribute for mutually exclusive panels. Supports single or multiple open panels. When should I use it? Use <Accordion> for FAQ sections, settings panels, or any grouped content where only one section should be visible at a time. For independent collapsible panels, use multiple <Panel> components. Why does it exist? Native HTML — <details> / <summary> for built-in keyboard and screen-reader support. Mutual exclusion — the native name attribute ensures only one panel is open. Progressive enhancement — works without JavaScript. Sources MDN — <details> WAI-ARIA APG — Accordion Primer — Accordion Material Design 3 — Expansion panels Ant Design — Collapse Twintrinsic Implementation Native `<details>` + `<summary>` for expand/collapse — zero JS `<details name="group">` for exclusive behavior (only one open at a time) `aria-expanded` on the summary button `aria-controls` linking the summary to the panel content CSS transitions for smooth expand/collapse animation Common Mistakes Don't use `<div onclick>` with a JS toggle — `<details>` is native and accessible Don't forget `<details name>` for exclusive accordion behavior Don't use Accordion for tab switching — use the Tabs component instead Related Components Tabs, Tree, Menu Responsiveness Full-width by default; set a max-width via `class` or a parent Container. Touch targets meet the 44×44 px minimum for the summary header. Customization allowMultiple — allow multiple panels open simultaneously. defaultExpanded — index of the initially expanded item, or null for all collapsed. bordered — show or hide the border. Custom header snippets per item. Examples Billing FAQ Is there a free trial? Yes — every new workspace starts with a 14-day free trial. When will I be billed? You'll be billed on the first day of each billing cycle. `}> Is there a free trial? Yes — every new workspace starts with a 14-day free trial. No credit card is required, and you can cancel anytime. When will I be billed? You'll be billed on the first day of each billing cycle. Invoices are emailed to the workspace owner. Can I change my plan later? ### /docs/components/Alert/Alert

Alert documentation page — standardized structure

Alert Alert displays inline notifications, important information, or warnings. It features a colored background with a thick one-side border for visual emphasis, and can be dismissed by the user when appropriate. What, When & Why What is it? An inline notification component that renders important information with visual emphasis. It uses a colored background and a thick border on one side to draw attention. Alerts can include an icon, title, and dismissible close button. When should I use it? Use <Alert> for contextual information that doesn't block the user's workflow: "You have 3 new messages", "Your account is almost full", informational callouts in page sections, or best-practices guidance. For blocking notifications that require user action, use <Modal> . For transient feedback, use <Toast> . Why does it exist? Visual emphasis — thick one-side border and colored background immediately draw attention. Non-blocking — inline content that doesn't interrupt the user's flow. Accessible — uses role="alert" for screen reader announcements. Flexible — four severity levels, customizable border side, optional dismiss. Responsiveness Full-width by default; use max-w-* classes to constrain. Text wraps naturally on narrow viewports. Close button meets 44×44 px touch target minimum. Customization Variants: info , success , warning , error , default . Border side: left , right , top , bottom . Optional title for bold heading text. Optional icon — auto-selected per variant, or custom Iconify name. dismissible prop adds a close button. Examples Variants A new version of the app is available for download. ### /docs/components/App/App

App documentation page — standardized structure

App App is the root layout component that establishes the page shell for every screen in your application. It composes a header, optional sidebar(s), main content area, and footer into a responsive grid, and sets up the semantic landmark structure ( <main> , <header> , <footer> ) that screen readers rely on for navigation. What, When & Why What is it? A layout wrapper that provides named slots for header, left panel, right panel, main content, footer, and an optional menu bar. It manages the CSS Grid that arranges these regions and reflows them for mobile viewports. When should I use it? Use <App> as the outermost component on every page. It is the structural foundation that all other layout components (AppHeader, Sidebar, Footer) slot into. If your app has a consistent page skeleton, this is it. Why does it exist? Jakob's Law — users expect your app to work like every other app they know. A predictable page skeleton (header top, nav left, content center, footer bottom) meets that expectation. Accessibility — proper landmark regions ( main , header , nav , footer ) let screen-reader users jump between page sections instantly. Responsive — the grid automatically collapses side panels on small screens so you don't have to write breakpoint logic in every page. Sources WAI-ARIA APG — Landmarks MDN — <main> Primer — PageLayout Twintrinsic Implementation Uses CSS Grid with `grid-template-rows` and `grid-template-columns` for the page shell Semantic `<main>` element for the content area Accepts `header`, `footer`, `leftPanel`, `rightPanel` snippets for flexible composition `<svelte:window>` for scroll event handling `data-theme` attribute on the root for theme propagation `...rest` spread for native attribute passthrough (`data-*`, `aria-*`) Common Mistakes Don't put navigation inside `<main>` — it belongs in `<nav>` within the header or sidebar Don't use `<div>` for the main content area — always use `<main>` for landmark semantics Don't forget `id="main-content"` for skip-nav links Related Components AppHeader, Sidebar, Footer, BottomBar, Container Responsiveness Desktop (≥ 640 px) — side panels sit beside the main content in a row layout. Mobile (< 640 px) — side panels expand to full width and stack vertically beneath the main content. Panel widths are configurable via the leftPanelWidth and rightPanelWidth props. Customization All spacing, colors, and typography inherit from the Tailwind theme in twintrinsic.css . Pass additional CSS classes via the class prop. Each slot accepts any Svelte content — there are no restrictions on what you place in the header, panels, or footer. Examples Basic Layout Projects Track and manage your team's work. `}> App Shell Preview This component is a full-page layout wrapper. See the code tab for the typical usage pattern. App Shell with a BottomBar A real app shell usually wants a bar along its bottom edge — a build console, a mobile tab bar, or media controls. BottomBar is prop-driven : the shell header owns the visibility, so clicking the action in the header below shows and hides the console through expanded — no internal toggle, no imperative call. The framed preview below stands in for the app viewport. In a real page you compose <App> with your content and place the docked BottomBar as its sibling so it pins to the window bottom. let consoleOpen = false <\/script> Projects (consoleOpen = !consoleOpen)}> Console ✓ Build completed successfully ⚠ 2 deprecation warnings `}> Acme Suite (consoleOpen = !consoleOpen)}> Website Redesign Updated 2 hours ago Mobile App Launch Updated yesterday Console ✓ Build completed successfully ⚠ 2 deprecation warnings Slots Slot Description default Main content area of the application header Application header area — typically an AppHeader leftPanel Left sidebar panel — typically a Sidebar rightPanel Right sidebar panel — optional secondary navigation footer Application footer area — typically a Footer menu Optional menu area above the header Props Accessibility Main content area uses the <main> element with role="main" . Footer uses the <footer> element. Document title is set automatically from the appName prop. All regions are exposed as ARIA landmarks so screen-reader users can jump directly to the header, navigation, main content, or footer. Keyboard Support The App component itself does not contain interactive elements. Keyboard support is handled by the components placed inside its slots (AppHeader, Sidebar, etc.).

### /docs/components/AppHeader/AppHeader

AppHeader documentation page — standardized structure

AppHeader AppHeader is the persistent top navigation bar for your application. It provides a home for your brand identity, primary navigation links, global search, notification bell, and user profile menu — all in a single, responsive component that collapses to a hamburger menu on mobile. What, When & Why What is it? A horizontal bar fixed to the top of the viewport containing (from left to right): brand logo/name, primary navigation links, a search input, notification icon, and user avatar/menu. On small screens the navigation collapses behind a hamburger button. When should I use it? Place <AppHeader> inside the header slot of <App> on every page. It is the standard entry point for top-level navigation, search, and account access. Why does it exist? Consistency — users expect a persistent top bar for orientation and navigation across every page (Jakob's Law). Discoverability — search, notifications, and profile are always in the same place, reducing cognitive load. Accessibility — uses <header> and <nav> landmarks so screen-reader users can jump directly to navigation. Sources WAI-ARIA APG — Landmarks MDN — <header> Primer — PageHeader Material Design 3 — Top app bar Responsiveness Desktop (≥ 640 px) — full navigation links visible, search input expanded. Mobile (< 640 px) — nav links collapse behind a hamburger menu button, search collapses to an icon, notification and user icons remain visible. Hamburger button uses aria-expanded and aria-controls for screen-reader toggle state. Touch targets meet the 44×44 px minimum for mobile tap areas. Customization Pass a string or a { name, logo, href } object as brand . Nav items accept label , href , and current properties. Override default search and notification behavior via the showSearch and showNotifications props. Custom content in the notifications and user-menu areas via named slots. Theme colors, spacing, and borders are controlled by the Tailwind theme. Examples Basic Header `}> With Logo `}> Full Featured `}> Slots Slot Description notifications Custom content for the notifications panel user-menu Custom content for the user dropdown menu Props Type Definitions Events Accessibility Uses the <header> landmark and <nav aria-label> for screen-reader navigation. Mobile hamburger toggle uses aria-expanded and aria-controls . All interactive elements are keyboard-focusable with visible focus rings. Dropdown menus trap focus and can be dismissed with Escape. Notification and user menu use aria-haspopup and aria-expanded . Keyboard Support Key Function Tab Moves focus through interactive elements in order Enter / Space Activates buttons, opens/closes dropdowns Escape Closes the mobile menu, notifications panel, and user menu Arrow Keys Navigates between nav items and dropdown menu items

### /docs/components/Avatar/Avatar

Avatar documentation page — standardized structure

Avatar Displays a user's profile image with intelligent fallback options — initials, Gravatar, or a generic icon. Supports sizes, shapes, status indicators, and notification badges. What, When & Why What is it? An image component that shows a user's profile picture, with automatic fallback to initials, Gravatar, or a placeholder icon when no image is available. When should I use it? Use <Avatar> anywhere you need to represent a person or entity visually — user lists, comments, team pages, chat messages, navigation bars. For groups of avatars, use <AvatarGroup> . Why does it exist? Consistent sizing — predefined sizes (xs, sm, md, lg, xl) keep avatars uniform. Graceful fallback — if the image fails to load, shows initials or a generic icon. Gravatar integration — generates a Gravatar URL from an email address. Status indicators — online/offline/away/busy dots with semantic colors. Sources Material Design 3 — Avatars Primer — Avatar MDN — img element Twintrinsic Implementation `<img>` with `alt` text for user avatars `aspect-ratio: 1` for consistent circular sizing Fallback to initials when no image is provided AvatarGroup with overlap using negative margin `<picture>` with `<source>` for AVIF/WebP responsive images Common Mistakes Don't forget `alt` text — even if decorative, use `alt=""` (empty alt) Don't use `<div>` for the image — always `<img>` for semantics Related Components Badge, Icon, Image Responsiveness Avatars are fixed-size by default; use size prop to control. In <AvatarGroup> , avatars overlap and adapt to container width. Customization Shapes: circle , square , rounded . Status indicators: online , offline , away , busy . Badge overlay for notification counts. Bordered and shadowed variants. Examples Basic Image `}> Fallback with Initials `}> Custom Fallback `}> Gravatar Email `}> Sizes `}> Shapes `}> Status Indicators `}> Badges `}> Styled Avatars `}> Props Accessibility Images have proper alt text. Status indicators include aria-label for screen readers. Fallback text is exposed to assistive technology. Color contrast meets WCAG AA standards. Fallback Behavior The Avatar has a priority chain: src — displays the image if it loads successfully. gravatarEmail — generates a Gravatar URL (SHA-256 + identicon fallback). fallback — displays the provided fallback text. name — auto-generates initials from the name. Generic user icon — if nothing else is available.

### /docs/components/Avatar/AvatarGroup

AvatarGroup documentation page — standardized structure

AvatarGroup Displays multiple avatars in a compact, overlapping stack. Supports a maximum visible count with an overflow counter. What, When & Why What is it? A layout container that renders child <Avatar> components in a horizontal stack with negative margins for overlap. When the number of children exceeds max , an overflow counter is shown. When should I use it? Use <AvatarGroup> to show a list of users who are assigned to or participating in something — task assignees, comment authors, team members. For a single avatar, use <Avatar> directly. Why does it exist? Space efficiency — overlapping avatars take less horizontal space. Overflow handling — the max prop truncates with a "+N" counter. Semantic grouping — renders role="group" with an accessible name. Sources Material Design 3 — Avatars Primer — Avatar Responsiveness Avatars overlap; the group width grows with the number of visible avatars. On narrow containers, the overflow counter handles remaining items. Customization max — maximum visible avatars before the overflow counter appears. total — total count (used in the overflow counter text). Child avatars inherit sizing and border styling from the group. Examples Basic Group `}> With Overflow Count `}> Props Accessibility Renders a role="group" container with an accessible name. Each avatar retains its own aria-label . The overflow counter text is exposed to screen readers.

Badge A small inline element for displaying counts, status indicators, or labels. Supports variants, sizes, dot indicators, pulse animation, and overlay positioning. What, When & Why What is it? ### /docs/components/BottomBar/BottomBar

BottomBar documentation page — standardized structure

BottomBar BottomBar is a bar that attaches to the bottom of its parent container. It is ideal for mobile app bars, media player controls, console output, detail panels, or any content that should be on hand but not always on screen. What, When & Why What is it? A bar anchored to the bottom edge of its parent. Its visibility is driven by the expanded prop, so another component's UX (a mobile menu button, a “show console” action, media playback state) decides when it appears. Set collapsible to let the header itself slide the bar down to a small handle and back. When should I use it? Use BottomBar for content that should be available on demand: a mobile app bar that appears when a menu opens, terminal/console output, media player controls, meeting control bars, or a collapsible detail panel in an editor. Why does it exist? Space efficiency — secondary content stays off screen until needed, maximizing the main content area. Thumb zones — on mobile, bottom-anchored controls are in the natural thumb reach zone (Steven Hoober research). Platform familiarity — bottom sheets and control bars are standard mobile UI patterns users already know. Sources Material Design 3 — Bottom sheets WAI-ARIA APG — Landmarks Primer — Overlay patterns Responsiveness Desktop — the bottom bar sits at the bottom of its parent container. Mobile — provides two modes: Float mode (default) — slides up as an overlay with a backdrop. Inline mode — pushes content up, taking full width. Touch targets meet the 44×44 px minimum for mobile tap areas. Customization Custom header via the header snippet (text, icons, or any markup). Show/hide from another component via the expanded prop. Let users collapse the bar to a small handle via collapsible . Set the bar height via the height prop. Theme colors, borders, and spacing controlled by the Tailwind theme. Pass additional CSS classes via the class prop. Examples Basic BottomBar A simple collapsible detail panel anchored to the bottom. Click the header to toggle. ### /docs/components/Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb

Breadcrumb documentation page — standardized structure

Breadcrumb Breadcrumb shows the user's current location within a site hierarchy as a trail of links. Uses native <nav> , <ol> , and <li> elements. What, When & Why What is it? A horizontal list of links separated by visual dividers. The last item represents the current page (not a link). Collapses middle items when the trail is long. When should I use it? Use on every page with 3+ levels of hierarchy. Place at the top of the content area. Not needed for single-level sites. Why does it exist? Orientation — helps users understand where they are in the site structure. Navigation — provides quick access to parent pages. Accessibility — <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> lets screen-reader users jump to the trail. Sources WAI-ARIA APG — Breadcrumb Primer — Breadcrumbs Twintrinsic Implementation Semantic `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` + `<ol>` + `<li>` structure `aria-current="page"` on the last link (current page) Separator styling via CSS `::before` pseudo-element — no JS needed `<link>` on each item except the last (which uses `<span>` or `<a aria-current="page">`) Common Mistakes Don't use `<div>` for breadcrumbs — always `<nav>` + `<ol>` for landmark semantics Don't forget `aria-current="page"` on the last item Related Components App, AppHeader, Sidebar, Tree Responsiveness Wraps naturally on narrow screens. Collapsible mode hides middle items on overflow. Customization Custom separator via separator prop. Collapsible via collapsible + maxVisibleItems . Icons on individual items. Examples Basic Breadcrumb Home Documentation Breadcrumb `}> Home Documentation Breadcrumb Custom Separator Home Documentation Breadcrumb `}> Home Documentation Breadcrumb Data-Driven (items prop) Instead of using <BreadcrumbItem> sub-components, you can pass a flat array of objects. This is simpler for generated or dynamic breadcrumbs. `}> Collapsible `}> With Icons Home Documentation Components `}> Home Documentation Components Breadcrumb Props BreadcrumbItem Props Accessibility Uses <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> . Ordered list ( <ol> ) for proper trail semantics. aria-current="page" on the current (last) item. Separators hidden from screen readers via aria-hidden .

BreadcrumbItem is a sub-component of Breadcrumb . See the parent component docs for usage, examples, and full API reference. BreadcrumbItem BreadcrumbItem is a single item within a Breadcrumb. ### /docs/components/Button/ButtonGroup

ButtonGroup documentation page — standardized structure

ButtonGroup ButtonGroup groups related Button components together with consistent spacing, connected corners, and shared styling. Variant and size can be set once on the group and are inherited by every child button. What, When & Why What is it? A layout wrapper that groups buttons into a visually connected unit with shared variant/size inheritance and connected corners. Uses role="group" with aria-label for accessibility. When should I use it? Use <ButtonGroup> for toolbars (bold/italic/underline), pagination, toggle groups, or any set of related buttons that should appear visually connected. Why does it exist? Visual grouping — connected corners and shared styling. Variant inheritance — set variant/size once for all child buttons. Accessible — role="group" with aria-label . ### /docs/components/Card/Card

Card documentation page — standardized structure

Card Card is a styled container for self-contained content with optional header, media, and footer sections. It renders as an <article> element, indicating that its content is independently meaningful. What, When & Why What is it? A content container that groups related information — headers, images, text, and actions — into a visually cohesive unit. Renders as <article> (or <a> when href is set) for correct semantics. When should I use it? Use <Card> for self-contained content that could stand alone: blog posts, product listings, user profiles, testimonials, dashboard widgets. For layout wrapping, use <Container> . For collapsible content, use <Panel> . Why does it exist? Semantic HTML — <article> signals self-contained content. Flexible slots — header, media, body, and footer for diverse content. Interactive — hoverable and href for clickable cards. Media images use object-cover for consistent aspect ratios. ### /docs/components/Carousel/Carousel

Carousel documentation page — standardized structure

Carousel Carousel is a slideshow for cycling through elements — images, cards, text, or custom markup. It supports various transition effects, navigation controls, and touch interactions. What, When & Why What is it? A content carousel with slide/fade transitions, prev/next arrows, dot indicators, and autoplay support. Uses CSS Scroll Snap for smooth swiping and ARIA tablist for accessibility. When should I use it? Use <Carousel> for image galleries, feature highlights, testimonials, or any content that benefits from sequential browsing. For data grids, use <DataTable> . Why does it exist? Touch-friendly — swipe gestures on mobile. Accessible — ARIA tablist with keyboard navigation. Flexible — slide or fade transitions, autoplay, custom arrows. Slide content should use explicit text colors (e.g., text-text dark:text-white ) for dark mode readability. ### /docs/components/Carousel/CarouselItem

CarouselItem documentation page — standardized structure

CarouselItem is a sub-component of Carousel . See the parent component docs for usage, examples, and full API reference. CarouselItem CarouselItem is a single slide inside a <Carousel> . It registers itself with the parent carousel and renders as a role="tabpanel" with aria-roledescription="slide" . What, When & Why What is it? A single slide within a Carousel. Each CarouselItem is a content panel that can contain images, text, cards, or any markup. The parent Carousel manages transitions, navigation, and active state. When should I use it? Always use <CarouselItem> inside a <Carousel> . Each slide in your carousel gets its own <CarouselItem> . Why does it exist? Self-contained slides — each item is an independent content panel. Accessible — role="tabpanel" with aria-roledescription="slide" . Flexible — accepts any content as children. Sources WAI-ARIA APG — Carousel Material Design 3 — Carousel Ant Design — Carousel MDN — tabpanel role Primer — Overlay Responsiveness Fills the carousel container width. Content scales naturally within the slide. Customization Accepts any content as children. Parent Carousel controls transition, arrows, and indicators. Examples Basic Slides Unlimited projects Real-time collaboration `}> Unlimited projects Create as many workspaces as you need. Real-time collaboration Edit together with your team, live. Enterprise security SOC 2, SSO, and role-based access. Fade Transition Slide 1 Slide 2 `}> Slide 1 Slide 2 No Controls Slide 1 Slide 2 `}> Slide 1 Slide 2 Props Events Accessibility Each slide renders role="tabpanel" with aria-roledescription="slide" . Inactive slides are hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden . Keyboard users navigate with Arrow keys, Home, and End on the carousel region. Keyboard Support CarouselItem is a content panel and does not require direct keyboard interaction. Navigation is handled by the parent Carousel.

### /docs/components/Chip/Chip

Chip documentation page — standardized structure

Chip A compact element for representing an input, attribute, or action. Chips support selection, removal, and click interactions with full keyboard navigation. What, When & Why What is it? A small, rounded element that can display text, icons, or avatars. Chips can be clickable (toggle selection), removable (with an × button), or static. When should I use it? Use <Chip> for selected filters, tag inputs, removable categories, or compact action buttons. For purely visual labels, use <Badge> . For dismissible labels in a group, use <Tag> . Why does it exist? Interactive selection — toggle chips on/off for filter states. Removable — users can dismiss chips with a clear × button. Rich content — supports icons and avatars inside the chip. Group management — <ChipGroup> handles layout and selection state. Sources Material Design 3 — Chips Primer — Toggle Button Ant Design — Tag Twintrinsic Implementation `<button>` for clickable chips (more interactive than Tag) `aria-pressed` for toggle chips `aria-live="polite"` for dynamic chip addition/removal Icons, avatars, and close buttons supported Common Mistakes Don't use `<span onclick>` — always `<button>` for interactive chips Don't forget `aria-pressed` for toggle state Related Components Tag, TagGroup, Button Responsiveness Chips wrap naturally within their container. In <ChipGroup> , chips use flexbox wrap layout. Customization Variants: default, primary, secondary, success, warning, error, info. Sizes: sm, md, lg. Style: outline for bordered chips. clickable — makes the chip a toggle button. removable — adds a dismiss × button. selected — reflects selection state. icon and avatar — rich content inside the chip. ### /docs/components/Chip/ChipGroup

ChipGroup documentation page — standardized structure

ChipGroup A container for managing multiple Chip components with consistent spacing, layout, and selection state. Supports listbox semantics for accessible selectable groups. What, When & Why What is it? A layout wrapper that arranges <Chip> components in a flex wrap container. When selectable , it tracks which chips are selected and provides keyboard navigation. When should I use it? Use <ChipGroup> when you need a set of selectable or removable chips — filter categories, skill tags, plan selectors. For a simple list of static chips, just use CSS flex wrap directly. Why does it exist? Centralized selection — tracks selected state for multiple chips. Listbox semantics — role="listbox" with aria-multiselectable . Dynamic items — render from a data array with itemTemplate . CodeBlock CodeBlock displays code snippets with syntax highlighting and copy functionality. It supports multiple programming languages, auto-detection, and Prism.js plugins. Use <CodeBlock> whenever you need to display code snippets to users: documentation, tutorials, blog posts, or developer tools. For code editing, use <CodeEditor> . Why does it exist? Syntax highlighting — Prism.js with on-demand grammar loading. Auto-detection — infers language from content when not specified. Copy button — one-click clipboard access. Plugin system — line numbers, toolbar, and more. When should I use it? Use <CodeBlockSpeed> for read-only code samples in documentation, blog posts, or tutorials where bundle size and rendering speed matter. ### /docs/components/Container/Container

Container documentation page — standardized structure

Container Container is a fundamental layout component that provides consistent padding and width constraints. It is designed to work seamlessly with Tailwind's responsive breakpoints and supports both fixed-width and fluid layouts. What, When & Why What is it? A polymorphic layout wrapper that renders as a semantic HTML element ( <section> , <main> , <article> , etc.) with responsive max-width constraints and padding. It is the foundation for page structure and section layout. When should I use it? Use <Container> to wrap page sections, control max-width, and add responsive padding. For self-contained content units (blog posts, product cards), use <Card> . For collapsible sections, use <Panel> . Why does it exist? Consistent spacing — responsive padding across all breakpoints. Polymorphic element — render as <main> , <section> , etc. for correct semantics. Fluid option — fluid mode for full-width layouts. Sources Tailwind CSS — Container Primer — Box Material Design 3 — Layout Ant Design — Layout MDN — <section> Twintrinsic Implementation Container: CSS Container Queries (`container-type: inline-size`) for responsive child styling Section: semantic `<section>` element with a heading Panel: `<div>` with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it is a landmark `...rest` spread for native attributes Common Mistakes Don't use `<div>` for Section — `<section>` is the correct semantic element Don't forget `<section>` needs a heading for proper semantics Related Components Card, App, Section Responsiveness Standard mode uses Tailwind's `container` class with responsive padding (`px-4` → `px-6` → `px-8`). Fluid mode is full-width with no max-width constraint. Customization as prop: "section", "main", "article", "div", "header", "footer", "nav", "aside". fluid for full-width layouts. role and ariaLabel for accessibility. Examples Basic Container Content in a basic container `}> Content in a basic container Fluid Container Content in a fluid container `}> Content in a fluid container Semantic Element `}> This renders as a <main> element with role="main" . When to Use Container vs Card vs Panel Component Use When HTML Element Container Page or section layout structure with responsive max-width <div> / semantic Card Self-contained, reusable content (blog post, product listing) <article> Panel Collapsible or expandable content (FAQ, settings) <details> Props Accessibility Use the as prop to render the correct semantic element ( <main> , <section> , etc.). Add role and ariaLabel when the element alone does not convey semantics. Container is a layout-only wrapper; use semantic elements inside it. Keyboard Support Container is a layout-only element and does not require keyboard interaction.

### /docs/components/EventsTable/EventsTable

EventsTable A utility component that renders a component's events (Svelte 5 callback props) as a documentation table. Like PropsTable , it reads the events directly from a component module's propsMetadata export (keeping the entries that dispatch a CustomEvent ), or renders a data hash as a fallback. Usage Auto-derived events Pass the component module to list its on* callback props that dispatch a CustomEvent : Explicit data hash When a component doesn't export propsMetadata , pass a plain data hash of event name → descriptor (names are written without the on prefix): Twintrinsic Implementation Native `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` for headers Auto-generated from TypeScript types via `propsMetadata` `<caption>` for table title `content-visibility: auto` for large tables Common Mistakes Don't use `<div>` — always `<table>` for semantic data display Don't forget `<th scope="col">` for column header associations Related Components DataTable, CompatibilityMatrix Props Accessibility Uses a semantic <table> with header cells for each column Event names are rendered as their on* callback prop form The table scrolls horizontally on narrow viewports instead of overflowing

### /docs/components/Footer/Footer

Footer documentation page — standardized structure

Footer Footer is a persistent bottom section for your page or application. It provides three flexible regions — left, center, and right — for copyright text, legal links, secondary navigation, and contact information. What, When & Why What is it? A horizontal bar using the native <footer> element with three snippet slots (left, center, right) that stack into a single centered column on small screens. When should I use it? Place <Footer> in the footer slot of <App> on every page. Use it for copyright notices, legal links, social media links, and contact information. Why does it exist? Convention — users expect to find legal info and secondary links at the bottom of every page (Jakob's Law). Accessibility — the native <footer> element creates a landmark that screen-reader users can jump to directly. Consistency — a single component ensures the same footer structure across every page. Sources WAI-ARIA APG — Landmarks MDN — <footer> Primer — PageLayout Twintrinsic Implementation Semantic `<footer>` element as root Three-region layout: `footer-left`, `footer-center`, `footer-right` via CSS flexbox Accepts `left`, `center`, `right` snippets for flexible content `...rest` spread on `<footer>` for native attributes Common Mistakes Don't put primary navigation in the footer — it belongs in the header or sidebar Don't use `<div>` — always `<footer>` for landmark semantics Don't forget the copyright year can be dynamic via JS Related Components App, AppHeader, Separator Responsiveness Desktop — left, center, and right regions are displayed in a horizontal row with appropriate spacing. Mobile (< 640 px) — regions stack vertically into a single centered column for readability. Empty regions are not rendered, so no stray whitespace appears. Customization Each region (left, center, right) accepts any Svelte content via snippets. Use the class prop to add custom Tailwind classes. Theme colors and borders are controlled by the Tailwind theme. Examples Three-Region Footer © 2026 Twintrinsic Privacy Policy · Terms Contact Us `}> © 2026 Twintrinsic Privacy Policy · Terms Contact Us Center-Only Footer Copyright © 2026 Twintrinsic `}> Copyright © 2026 Twintrinsic Slots Slot Description left Left-aligned content (copyright, version info) center Center-aligned content (legal links, secondary nav) right Right-aligned content (contact info, social links) Props Accessibility Uses the native <footer> element, which automatically creates an ARIA landmark. Screen-reader users can jump directly to the footer using landmark navigation. Links inside the footer are standard <a> elements with full keyboard support. Keyboard Support The Footer component itself does not contain custom interactive elements. Keyboard support is handled by the standard <a> links placed inside its slots.

### /docs/components/Form/Calendar

Calendar documentation page — standardized structure

Calendar Calendar is a date picker built on the native <input type="date"> element. It uses the browser's built-in date picker for accessibility, validation, and localized formatting — free of charge. What, When & Why What is it? A form control that lets users pick a date using the browser's native date picker. Provides a calendar popup, keyboard navigation, and locale-aware formatting with zero JavaScript overhead. When should I use it? Use <Calendar> when the user needs to pick a single date. The native picker provides ARIA support, keyboard navigation, and validation for free. For date range selection, use two Calendar components side by side. For custom calendar grids with week numbers or blocked dates, consider a dedicated calendar library. Why does it exist? Accessible by default — native date pickers have built-in ARIA, keyboard navigation, and screen reader support. Locale-aware — the browser formats dates according to the user's locale automatically. Validated — min / max attributes prevent invalid dates natively. Lightweight — no custom calendar grid JavaScript needed. ### /docs/components/Form/Checkbox

Checkbox documentation page — standardized structure

Checkbox Checkbox is a form control for toggling between two states (checked/unchecked) or three states (checked/unchecked/indeterminate). It wraps the native <input type="checkbox"> with consistent styling, labels, descriptions, and validation support. What, When & Why What is it? A toggle control that lets the user select or deselect an option. Supports binary (on/off) and tri-state (on/off/partial) modes. The tri-state variant is useful for parent checkboxes that control a group of child checkboxes. When should I use it? Use <Checkbox> for independent binary choices — "Remember me", "I agree to terms", "Enable feature X". For mutually exclusive choices (exactly one must be selected), use <Radio> . For on/off settings that take effect immediately, consider <Switch> . Why does it exist? Native features — the underlying <input type="checkbox"> provides built-in toggle behavior, form participation, and screen reader support. Tri-state support — the indeterminate state is useful for "select all" patterns where some (but not all) children are checked. Consistency — ensures all checkboxes across the app share the same styling, label positioning, and error display. Touch targets meet 44×44 px minimum for mobile tap areas. Use size prop ("sm", "md", "lg") to adjust for different contexts. Customization Size: sm , md (default), or lg . Add descriptive text below the label via the description prop. Use accent-color (set in twintrinsic.css ) for brand-consistent check colors. Group checkboxes with <FormField> for shared labels and validation. Examples Basic Usage `}> With Description `}> Indeterminate State `}> Required `}> Required with Error `}> Disabled States `}> Checkbox Group `}> Slots The Checkbox component does not expose named slots. Use props for customization. For complex label content, use a raw <input type="checkbox"> with a <label> . Props Events Accessibility Uses native <input type="checkbox"> for maximum compatibility. Labels are properly associated via for / id attributes. Error messages linked via aria-describedby . Invalid states use aria-invalid="true" . Indeterminate state is set programmatically (not via HTML attribute). Keyboard Support Key Function Space Toggle checkbox state Tab Move focus to the checkbox

### /docs/components/Form/Combobox

Combobox documentation page — standardized structure

Combobox Combobox combines a text input with a dropdown list, providing autocomplete functionality. Users type to filter suggestions, then select from the filtered list. Uses popover="auto" for the dropdown panel with CSS Anchor Positioning for tethering. What, When & Why What is it? An editable text input with an associated popup that filters options as the user types. The popup uses the Popover API for top-layer rendering and light-dismiss. When should I use it? Use <Combobox> when users need to filter a large dataset while typing (country selector, search with suggestions). For simple dropdown selection without typing, use <Select> . For action menus, use <Dropdown> . Why does it exist? Type-ahead filtering — narrows options as the user types, faster than scrolling. Rich options — options can include icons, flags, descriptions. Popover API — light-dismiss, top-layer, and CSS Anchor Positioning with zero JS. ### /docs/components/Form/Dropdown

Dropdown documentation page — standardized structure

Dropdown Dropdown is a menu-based selection component for choosing one or multiple options from a list. It supports icons, option groups, cascading submenus, filtering, and keyboard navigation. What, When & Why What is it? A button that opens a menu of options when clicked. Different from Select in that it's primarily designed for actions and rich option content (icons, nested groups) rather than plain value selection. When should I use it? Use <Dropdown> for action menus (edit, delete, share) or for option selection with rich content (icons, descriptions). For simple value selection, prefer <Select> . For type-ahead filtering, use <Combobox> . Why does it exist? Rich content — options can include icons, descriptions, and nested groups. Space efficient — collapses many options into a single button. Popover API — uses popover="auto" for top-layer rendering, light-dismiss, and zero-JS open/close. Filterable options via filter= . Clearable selection. Sizes: sm , md , lg . ### /docs/components/Form/FloatLabel

FloatLabel documentation page — standardized structure

FloatLabel FloatLabel wraps form inputs with an animated label that floats above the field when focused or filled, saving vertical space while maintaining clear context. What, When & Why What is it? A form field wrapper that positions the label inside the input when empty, then animates it above the input when focused or filled. Uses CSS :has() for the float animation — no JavaScript needed. When should I use it? Use <FloatLabel> for dense forms where vertical space is at a premium: mobile forms, side panels, modal forms. Persistent context — the floating label is always visible, even after typing. Modern CSS — :has() enables the float animation without JS. ### /docs/components/Form/Form

Form documentation page — standardized structure

Form Form is a container component that provides form submission, validation, layout, and state management. FormField wraps individual inputs with labels, help text, and error messages. What, When & Why What is it? <Form> handles submission, validation, disabled/loading states, and layout (vertical or horizontal). <FormField> wraps each input with a label, help text, error message, and required indicator. When should I use it? Wrap every form in <Form> . Wrap every input in <FormField> — even simple fields benefit from consistent label positioning and error display. Why does it exist? Consistency — all forms share the same validation, error display, and layout. Accessibility — <fieldset> + <legend> for groups, aria-describedby for error messages. Developer ergonomics — programmatic API for reset, validate, setValues, setErrors. Twintrinsic Implementation FormField wraps inputs with label, helper text, and error message `:has(:user-valid)` / `:has(:user-invalid)` for CSS-only validation styling `aria-describedby` links input to error/helper text `aria-invalid` on the input when validation fails Form context via `setContext('form')` / `getContext('form')` for shared state Common Mistakes Don't show error messages on mount — use `:user-valid`/`:user-invalid` to show after interaction Don't forget `aria-describedby` — screen readers need the error message linked to the input Related Components Input, Checkbox, Select, InvalidState Responsiveness Vertical layout (default) stacks fields vertically. Horizontal layout ( layout="horizontal" ) places labels beside inputs on desktop, stacks on mobile. Customization Layout: vertical (default) or horizontal . States: disabled , loading , validate . FormField: label , helpText , error , required , hideLabel . Examples Basic Form Submit `}> Submit Horizontal Layout Submit `}> Submit Form States Submit `}> Submit Validation Submit `}> Submit Form Props FormField Props Events Accessibility Labels associated via for / id . Required fields use aria-required . Error messages use role="alert" and aria-describedby . Disabled state communicated via aria-disabled .

### /docs/components/Form/FormBuilder

FormBuilder documentation page — standardized structure

FormBuilder FormBuilder generates an accessible form from an OpenAPI 3.0 Schema Object or an explicit field-descriptor array. It maps each schema property onto the matching Twintrinsic control, wires up labels, help text, and native validation, and renders everything inside a <Form> so submission "just works". What, When & Why What is it? A declarative form generator: give it a schema, get a complete, accessible form back. Every field gets a FormField wrapper (label, required indicator, help text, error styling), and the generated controls register with the Form context so native validation and the submit payload are handled for you. When should I use it? When your form's shape comes from data — an API contract, a config document, or a JSON schema your backend already publishes. For hand-crafted forms with bespoke layouts, compose Form + FormField + the individual controls directly instead. Why does it exist? Single source of truth — the schema drives the UI, so the form can never drift from the API contract. Accessible by construction — labels, aria-required , and error wiring come from the field metadata automatically. Composable — the generated controls are the same public components you'd write by hand. Schema Mapping The OpenAPI types map onto controls as follows: Schema Control string TextInput ( format: email → email, password → password) string + enum Select integer / number NumberInput ( minimum / maximum / multipleOf → min/max/step) boolean Switch array ListInput (or Select multiple when items.enum is present) object Nested <fieldset> group title → label (falling back to a humanized property name), description → help text, default → initial value, and the required list → required markers. References & Composition Pass the OpenAPI document's components.schemas map via the components prop to resolve $ref s. The resolver also handles the composition keywords: $ref — JSON-pointer references ( #/components/schemas/Pet ) are followed, including nested paths; unresolvable or circular references degrade to a plain text field instead of failing. allOf — subschemas are merged into one field set (properties, required list, bounds, enum). oneOf / anyOf — the first variant with a concrete type is rendered. References & allOf `} > Examples From an OpenAPI Schema `}> Field Descriptors Prefer explicit control? Pass a fields array — it takes precedence over schema : `}> Seeded Values `}> Without a Submit Button `}> Submit Handler }\n/>`} > } /> Props Events Accessibility Every generated field is wrapped in a FormField with a real <label> targeting the control. Required fields get aria-required and a visible asterisk; error states apply aria-invalid + an aria-live message. Object groups render as semantic <fieldset> / <legend> so nested fields are announced as a group. Native validation means keyboard and screen-reader behavior matches the platform. Limitations oneOf / anyOf render the first concrete variant rather than a discriminator-driven choice. Relative external $ref s (files/URLs) are not fetched — provide them via components . For deeply custom layouts, compose the controls directly instead.

For complex field groups (radio groups, checkbox groups), use <fieldset> + <legend> . Why does it exist? Consistency — all fields share the same label position, error style, and spacing. Accessibility — proper <label> association, aria-describedby for help/error text. Validation CSS — :has(:user-valid) / :has(:user-invalid) shows validation only after user interaction. Responsiveness Fills container width by default. Horizontal layout places labels beside inputs on desktop. Customization Layout: vertical (default) or horizontal . Help text via helpText prop. Error message via error prop. Required indicator via required prop. Visually hidden label via hideLabel prop.
